summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, transfusion-dependent anemia likely due to myelodysplastic syndrome, and recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin was admitted with acute-on-chronic left chest and shoulder pain and hypoxia. She was found to have volume overload contributing to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, evidenced by pleural effusions, crackles on exam, and elevated liver enzymes, managed with IV furosemide and transition to home torsemide. A catheter-associated urinary tract infection with Citrobacter amalonaticus and Enterococcus was treated with IV ceftriaxone, then oral cefpodoxime and amoxicillin based on sensitivities. Her INR was subtherapeutic at 1.2, so she was bridged with enoxaparin and warfarin, achieving a therapeutic INR of 2.4 at discharge. She received one unit of packed red blood cells for symptomatic anemia. A brief episode of symptomatic bradycardia was attributed to a vasovagal event and resolved spontaneously. She was discharged home with home health services on a 7-day antibiotic course, continued anticoagulation, and instructions to monitor weight and follow up with her providers.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
